edges.description: The tumour that triggers the syndrome is the same tumour that is its fourth diagnostic criterion, so this edge records how the mechanism becomes a recorded clinical feature rather than a causal step within the nervous system. It is the only route by which the Neuroblastoma phenotype enters the graph.

The trigger is followed by a humoral immune response within the central nervous system. The antigen that connects them is not known, which is why the steps are unspecified. Once started, the response does not depend on the tumour: resection and chemotherapy did not alter the cerebrospinal fluid abnormalities.

edges.description: A preceding infection is followed by the same intrathecal humoral response seen in the tumour-associated form. The steps between are unknown, as they are for the tumour trigger, and no cited source shows the two routes converging by the same molecular path.
edges.target: Intrathecal B-Cell Expansion and Oligoclonal IgG Synthesis

edges.description: An intrathecal humoral response is followed by cerebellar and brainstem dysfunction. No antigen or effector mechanism linking them is established. The cerebrospinal fluid lymphocyte abnormalities correlate with neurological severity, and patient IgG binds the neuronal surface in a minority of cases.
edges.source: Intrathecal B-Cell Expansion and Oligoclonal IgG Synthesis

edges.description: Loss of the omnipause and burst neuron balance produces back-to-back multidirectional saccades.
Arrhythmic action myoclonus of trunk and limbs.
Cerebellar ataxia, typically truncal, with dysarthria.

Behavioural change is part of the syndrome: mood and behaviour are scored on its severity scale, and the consensus review treats residual behavioural symptoms as possibly caused by the inflammation. Its anatomical basis is not established in the sources cited here.
Sleep disruption is part of the syndrome; as with the behavioural change, no mechanism is established here.
Dysarthria is the other cerebellar sign, listed with trunk ataxia in the syndrome description.

Atrophy of the vermis and hemispheres appears on imaging years after the acute phase, particularly after severe presentations, and correlates with a higher disease score, so it is read as a late structural consequence of the same injury the raised neurofilament light chain marks. No cited source follows an individual child from the biochemical marker to the structural change.

The neurofilament light chain result is read by its authors as neuronal or axonal injury, and the course of the illness tracks the outcome: more relapses go with a poorer cognitive outcome and remission with a better one, while features at presentation do not predict it. The link is still inferential: no cited source relates the marker, or any measure of the cerebellar and brainstem injury, to later cognitive scores.

Language is impaired during the untreated illness, where parents place the loss of speech after the first ataxic and myoclonic signs, and speech problems accompany the cognitive sequelae in follow-up. Speech is also one of the categories of the disease's severity scale. As with the cognitive edge, the connection to the acute injury is inferred: no cited source relates the neurofilament result to language measures.

Loss of already-acquired motor and language skills during the illness, related to age at presentation. The age dependence suggests the injury acts on skills in the course of being consolidated, but no cited source establishes that mechanism.

nodes.description: Cerebellar ataxia, characteristically truncal, often with dysarthria. The syndrome sits within the acquired cerebellar ataxias of childhood and is distinguished within them by opsoclonus and myoclonus and by the neuroblastoma association.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: OMAS falls along the spectrum of acquired cerebellar ataxias of childhood, which may include syndromes presenting purely with ataxia, but is distinct for its paraneoplastic association with neuroblastoma (26%-44%)6,7,10 and the presence of opsoclonus and myoclonus.

nodes.description: A late imaging finding rather than an acute one. Brain imaging is typically normal during the acute illness; atrophy of the cerebellar vermis and hemispheres has been described years later, particularly after severe presentations, and atrophy correlates with a higher disease score.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Cerebellar atrophy of the vermis and hemispheres has been described in patients who had follow-up imaging years after the acute phase, particularly in children who had severe presentations.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Neuroimaging of the brain is typically normal in the acute phase of OMAS, although cerebellar atrophy and cortical volume loss are occasionally seen longitudinally, and atrophy correlates with a higher OMAS score.

evidence.reference_title: Predictors of underlying neuroblastoma and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
evidence.snippet: All 73 patients underwent cranial MRI at onset. Imaging reports were summarized for 28 patients whose original images were unavailable, while the original imaging data were re-analyzed for 45 patients whose original images could be obtained. Cranial MRI findings were normal in all patients.

nodes.description: The clinical signs localise to the cerebellum and brainstem. Opsoclonus is attributed to instability in the balance between the brainstem omnipause and burst neurons that normally generate saccades; the ataxia and dysarthria are cerebellar. Cerebrospinal fluid neurofilament light chain was raised by 83 per cent in untreated patients and fell by 60 per cent to control levels on combination immunotherapy, which the authors read as neuronal or axonal injury that sufficient treatment reduces.

evidence.reference_title: Eye Movement Disorders in Movement Disorders.
evidence.snippet: thought that opsoclonus is attributed to instability in the fine balance between the omnipause and burst neurons in the brainstem that normally generate the saccadic eye movements

evidence.reference_title: CSF neurofilament light chain is elevated in OMS (decreasing with immunotherapy) and other pediatric neuroinflammatory disorders.
evidence.snippet: Only CSF NFL was elevated in untreated OMS versus controls (+83%). It was 87% higher in OIND than in OMS. On combination treatment with front-loaded ACTH, IVIg, rituximab, median CSF NFL decreased by 60% to control levels.

nodes.description: The outcome that matters most, and the reason the consensus review argues for early aggressive immunotherapy. Long-term cognitive and speech sequelae are reported in up to 75 per cent, good cognitive outcome in only 10 to 50 per cent of older series, and the range includes intellectual disability, specific learning disability, and deficits in attention, expressive language and visuospatial function even at normal IQ. What those figures do not settle is the course under treatment; the long-term phase in progression carries the one prospectively treated cohort, in which function was stable rather than declining.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Long-term sequelae including cognitive impairment and speech problems may be seen in up to 75% of patients but may potentially be mitigated by earlier and more aggressive immunotherapy.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: The range of cognitive and behavioural sequelae in children with OMAS includes intellectual disability, specific learning disabilities such as dyslexia, as well deficits in attention, expressive language, visuospatial function, and behavioral dysregulation, even in children with normal IQ.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term neurological outcomes of children with neuroblastoma with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome.
evidence.snippet: approximately 50–90% of children with OMS-NB have persistent neurological problems, such as late cognitive and neuropsychological sequelae, even after immunological and oncological treatment

nodes.description: Corticosteroids or adrenocorticotropic hormone are first-line immunotherapy. Two common corticosteroid regimens are pulsed intravenous methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisolone, or pulsed oral dexamethasone, with several alternatives in use. The claim that ACTH is superior to corticosteroids is not well supported, though the expert panel notes some refractory patients respond to it; corticosteroids are oral and cheaper.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Although some providers and studies have suggested that ACTH is superior to corticosteroids, little evidence supports this.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Treatment is largely predicated on immune suppression, but there is limited evidence to indicate an optimal regimen.

nodes.description: Children lose motor and language skills they had already acquired, and how much they lose is related to how old they were at presentation. This is distinct from the failure to acquire skills on time, and it is what makes the acute illness a developmental event rather than only a neurological one.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Many children lose previously acquired motor and language skills, with this regression related to age at presentation.

nodes.description: Dysarthria accompanies the truncal ataxia as the other cerebellar sign, and is listed with it in the syndrome description of the paraneoplastic criteria. Loss of speech is also one of the signs parents are asked to rank when the order of onset is reconstructed.

evidence.reference_title: Updated Diagnostic Criteria for Paraneoplastic Neurologic Syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Additional features include cerebellar involvement (dysarthria and trunk ataxia) and encephalopathy (ranging from confusion to coma).

nodes.description: The immune abnormality is intrathecal and would be missed by routine tests. Cerebrospinal fluid leukocyte counts are normal or barely raised and commercial serum autoantibody panels are negative, while in a cross-sectional cohort of 389 children cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands were present in 58 per cent and an expanded B-cell frequency in 93 per cent of untreated patients. Oligoclonal bands are not a consistent finding: a Chinese single-centre series found them in 1 of 21 children tested. The expansion is in cerebrospinal fluid and not blood, it correlates with neurological severity, and it persisted years after onset and conventional treatment. In children with neuroblastoma, resecting the tumour or giving chemotherapy did not alter the immunological abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: Demographic, Clinical, and Immunologic Features of 389 Children with Opsoclonus-Myoclonus Syndrome: A Cross-sectional Study.
evidence.snippet: The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leukocyte count was minimally elevated in 14% (<=11/mm3) with normal differential, and commercially screened serum autoantibodies were negative, but CSF oligoclonal bands (OCB) and B cells frequency were positive (58 and 93%).

evidence.reference_title: B- and T-cell markers in opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: immunophenotyping of CSF lymphocytes.
evidence.snippet: Abnormalities correlated with neurologic severity, as scored blinded from videotapes using a 12-item motor scale, and disease duration. No significant differences were found between tumor and no-tumor groups. In children with neuroblastoma, tumor resection or cancer chemotherapy did not alter immunologic abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: B- and T-cell markers in opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: immunophenotyping of CSF lymphocytes.
evidence.snippet: Although most children with OMS had normal CSF cell counts, they exhibited expansion of CD19+ B-cell (up to 29%) and gammadelta T-cell (up to 26%) subsets and a lower percentage of CD4+ T-cells and CD4/CD8 ratio, which persisted even years after disease onset and conventional treatments.

evidence.reference_title: Predictors of underlying neuroblastoma and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
evidence.snippet: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed minimal elevation in white blood cell (WBC) counts in both OMS subgroups, with all values ≤8/mm3.

evidence.reference_title: Predictors of underlying neuroblastoma and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
evidence.snippet: Intrathecal oligoclonal band (OCB) production was detected in only one patient without NB.

nodes.description: The only randomised prospective therapeutic trial in this disease. Children with neuroblastoma-associated opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia were randomised to prednisone and risk-adapted chemotherapy with or without intravenous immunoglobulin. Response was 21 of 26 (80.8 per cent) with it against 11 of 27 (40.7 per cent) without. Before this trial, treatment rested on case reports. Typical dosing is 2 g/kg over 2 to 5 days then 1 to 2 g/kg every 4 weeks for up to a year.

evidence.reference_title: Intravenous immunoglobulin with prednisone and risk-adapted chemotherapy for children with opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia syndrome associated with neuroblastoma (ANBL00P3): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: Significantly higher rates of OMA response were observed in patients randomized to IVIG+ compared to NO-IVIG [21/26=80.8% for IVIG+; 11/27=40.7% for NO-IVIG (odds ratio=6.1; 95% CI: (1.5, 25.9), p=0.0029)].

evidence.reference_title: Intravenous immunoglobulin with prednisone and risk-adapted chemotherapy for children with opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia syndrome associated with neuroblastoma (ANBL00P3): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: No previous clinical trial has been conducted for patients with neuroblastoma associated opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia syndrome (OMA), and current treatment is based on case reports.

therapeutic_agents: pooled human immunoglobulin G for intravenous use

nodes.description: Behavioural abnormality is one of the four diagnostic features, grouped with sleep disturbance in the criteria. Named specifically, it is irritability, sleep disturbance and inconsolable crying, and the group is frequent, in over half of patients. It is a non-motor feature and may appear in the absence of the full motor triad. It also bears on treatment: the irritability is why many children do not tolerate rehabilitation therapy early in the course.

evidence.snippet: Behavioral abnormalities, including sleep disturbance, irritability, and inconsolable crying, are frequent (over half of patients).

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis can be made when 3 of the following 4 features are present: (1) opsoclonus, (2) ataxia or myoclonus, (3) behavior change or sleep disturbance, and (4) neuroblastoma.1

nodes.description: Arrhythmic action myoclonus, predominantly of the trunk and limbs, and sometimes the head. It is one of the cardinal motor features and may appear separately from or together with the others.

evidence.reference_title: Updated Diagnostic Criteria for Paraneoplastic Neurologic Syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (OMS) is characterized by involuntary, high-frequency, chaotic multidirectional saccadic movements without intersaccadic pauses, and nonrhythmic action myoclonus, often involving the trunk, limbs, and head.

nodes.description: In about half of children a peripheral neuroblastic tumour is found, neuroblastoma in 73 per cent of those, ganglioneuroblastoma in 22 per cent and ganglioneuroma in 4 per cent. The tumours lie along the sympathetic chain or in the adrenals and are never intracranial, and 93 per cent of the neuroblastomas are stage 1 or 2; in a Chinese single-centre series all 30 tumours were localised, INRGSS stage L1 or L2, at diagnosis. In the other half no tumour is found; occult tumour with spontaneous regression has been proposed, and no clinical feature distinguishes the two groups. The parainfectious trigger below is the alternative route to the same immune node, and the two are not mutually exclusive.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Neuroblastoma (73%) is the most common tumor type, followed by ganglioneuroblastoma (22%) and ganglioneuroma (4%). The tumors are never in the brain: all are located along the sympathetic chain or in the adrenals, including the neck, thoracic, abdominal, or pelvic cavities.9 Notably, 93% of neuroblastoma is early stage (stage 1 or 2) in this population.9

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: Peripheral neuroblastic tumors are identified in 50% of children with OMAS,9 and some have suggested the presence of occult tumor in many more, with spontaneous regression in these cases.14 No clinical characteristics distinguish children with OMAS with and without occult tumor.8

evidence.reference_title: Predictors of underlying neuroblastoma and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
evidence.snippet: No patient exhibited distant metastasis at the time of initial tumor diagnosis. According to the INRGSS, 57% (n = 17) of patients were classified as stage L1, with 43% (n = 13) of patients were categorized as stage L2.

nodes.description: An underlying neuroblastoma is the fourth diagnostic feature. It is found in about half of children, reported between 26 and 50 per cent across sources, and conversely the syndrome occurs in 2 to 3 per cent of children with neuroblastoma. Where a tumour is found it is almost always early stage.

evidence.snippet: In 50% of children with OMS, a neuroblastoma (NB) is detected (2); this condition is called NB with OMS (OMS-NB), and OMS occurs in 2-3% of children with NB (3).

nodes.description: Spontaneous, arrhythmic, large-amplitude conjugate saccades in all directions of gaze with no intersaccadic interval. The absence of an intersaccadic interval is what distinguishes it from nystagmus, which is rhythmic. As it settles it may become ocular flutter, bursts of horizontal bidirectional back-to-back saccades, and the two can co-occur.

evidence.snippet: As it settles, opsoclonus may metamorphose into ocular flutter (bursts of horizontal bidirectional back-to-back saccades without an intersaccadic interval), and opsoclonus and ocular flutter can co-occur in many instances.

nodes.description: In the children in whom no tumour is found, an infection often precedes onset. No single organism accounts for it: Mycoplasma, Streptococcus, Epstein-Barr virus, adenovirus, human immunodeficiency virus and dengue virus have all been reported. An infectious prodrome does not point away from a tumour, because it occurs in children who turn out to have one, which is why every child presenting with the syndrome is screened regardless. In a Chinese single-centre series parents reported a prodromal infection for 51 per cent of children without a tumour and 37 per cent of those with one, a difference that was not significant, and testing found no consistent infectious agent.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: A variety of infections have been reported in association with OMAS, including Mycoplasma, Streptococcus, Epstein-Barr virus, adenovirus, HIV, and dengue virus, among others,16 suggesting that no single etiologic infectious agent exists.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: as an infectious prodrome may occur even in children with underlying tumor,9 all children presenting with OMAS should be screened for peripheral neuroblastic tumor.

evidence.reference_title: Predictors of underlying neuroblastoma and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
evidence.snippet: Parent-reported histories of prodromal infections were evaluated, which were present in 37% (n = 11) of the OMS with NB group and 51% (n = 22) of the OMS without NB group. No significant difference was found in the proportion of prodromal infections between the two groups.

evidence.reference_title: Predictors of underlying neuroblastoma and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
evidence.snippet: Although some patients underwent testing for a range of infectious agents, no consistent or specific infectious etiology was identified through clinical or laboratory assessments.

nodes.description: B-cell depletion, used in the aggressive multi-agent approach and as escalation in the stepwise one. The supporting evidence is indirect: an open-label study of 12 patients suggesting fewer relapses when combined with ACTH and immunoglobulin, higher IQ in a modern cohort where most received it against a historical cohort where none did, and shorter corticosteroid and immunoglobulin exposure in those given it. One study found better outcomes when it was given within 12 months of onset.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: The potential effectiveness of rituximab in OMAS is supported by (1) an open-label study of 12 patients suggesting a reduction in relapse rate when combined with ACTH and IVIg,50 (2) higher IQ in a modern cohort (in which 11/15 received rituximab) compared with a historical cohort (in which 0/23 received rituximab),4 and (3) reduction in the duration of corticosteroid and IVIg treatment in those given rituximab.48

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective.
evidence.snippet: One study showed that 15 patients who received rituximab within 12 months of OMAS onset were more likely to achieve a good response (defined as modified Rankin score 0-2) compared with 16 patients who received it later.5

nodes.description: Language is impaired in two distinguishable ways, and the binding is the tense-neutral term because the sources describe both. During the untreated illness children lack vocabulary and cannot form sentences, which the cross-sectional study assessed as delayed, and loss of speech is one of the ten characteristic signs whose order of appearance that study asked parents to rank. In follow-up, speech problems travel with the cognitive sequelae, and expressive language is among the specific deficits reported even at normal IQ. The acute loss of already-acquired language is recorded separately as developmental regression.
